### The Almighty One
Author: Chuck Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/todays-insight-september-3-2024.html
Passage: Genesis 17:1
Points:
- Thirteen years of divine silence followed Abram's failed human attempt to fulfill God's promise through Hagar.
- Waiting brought Abram to the end of his self-reliance, prompting quiet humility before the Lord.
- God reintroduced Himself as El-Shaddai to remind Abram of His supreme power and enduring presence.
- Even when God seems silent or distant, He remains fully in control of our circumstances.

### Walk Before Me and Be Blameless
Author: Eric Watkins
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/walk-me-and-be-blameless
Passage: Genesis 17:1
Points:
- God appeared to Abram in a vulnerable state of prolonged waiting, showing His timing rarely matches ours.
- Revealing Himself as El Shaddai highlights God's sovereign power over nature, including the barren womb.
- The command to walk blamelessly is a grateful response to covenant grace, not an effort to earn it.
- Human striving cannot accomplish God's promise; believers must learn to walk by faith rather than sight.
- The identity shift foreshadows Christ, who secures covenant blessings and empowers believers to live blamelessly.
